item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is the preferable patch because it keeps replay handling localized to FilesService and centralizes request construction, while A introduces a broad, contract-prohibited RawClient retry/body-ownership refactor. B still needs contract-alignment work before merge.","reasons":["B reuses multipartbody.NewFile and shares option handling, request construction, response decoding, and errors through one add helper; A duplicates the full Add implementation inside Upload and calls Raw.Do directly.","B’s retry test uses an open file and verifies multipart field name, filename, and content on both attempts, closely matching the reported streamed-upload failure.","A changes RawClient behavior for every seekable request body, including Content-Length calculation and caller ownership/closing semantics. This is unrelated global machinery explicitly outside the frozen scope.","A’s GetBody closure mutates and reuses one io.ReadSeeker across attempts, adding subtle redirect/concurrency and seek-state risks that the localized buffering approach avoids."],"risks_a":["Upload does not route through FilesService.Add and duplicates its request/response logic.","The global seekable-body implementation changes Files.Update, Persons.AddPicture, and arbitrary RawClient calls beyond the requested scope.","If seeking to the end fails after changing position, wireSeekableRequestBody returns without restoring the original offset; the changelog also advertises broad behavior outside the contract scope and tests do not cover source-reader errors."],"risks_b":["Add now eagerly buffers every custom multipart body, changing the preserved lower-level API’s streaming, memory, reader-error, and reader-closing behavior.","Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the existing public Add method, contrary to the contract’s explicit routing requirement.","The diff contains no explicit empty-filename or nil-content checks and adds no validation or source-reader-error tests."]}
